summary: Burst p99 latency spikes on Dedicated chat traffic (suspected KV cache fragmentation / allocator churn)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports burst-driven p99 latency spikes (10–30s) on Dedicated capacity in us-east during mixed-length chat traffic. Median latency stable, but tail degrades sharply during bursts and high request churn.

Customer impact
- Production user-facing chat product experiences timeouts + retries when bursts happen (customer sees elevated 5xx from their upstream due to timeouts).
- Customer SLO target: p99 < 2.5s for streaming-first response; currently p99 intermittently 12–28s during bursts.

Customer environment
- Customer: Northwind Analytics
- Tier: Dedicated
- Region: us-east
- Workload: chat completions, mixed prompt lengths (short prompts + occasional long context ~8k tokens), sustained decode with bursty arrival
- Runtime: runtime-1.21.x (customer pool) at time of initial report
- Client behavior: retries after 12s; concurrency spikes at top-of-hour batch jobs

Symptoms observed (initial)
- Tail latency spikes correlate with GPU memory pressure events, allocator stalls, and opportunistic KV evictions.
- No evidence of network/TLS issues; primarily runtime scheduling/allocator behavior.

Reproduction hints provided by customer
- Burst traffic: 4–6x baseline QPS for 2–4 minutes, repeated 1–3 times/hour
- Mixed sequence lengths: ~70% short, ~25% medium, ~5% long contexts

Diagnostics requested
1) Request IDs + timestamps for worst spikes
2) Response headers (x-redwood-request-id / model / region)
3) Any client-side timeouts / retry counts

Internal investigation notes
- Suspected KV arena fragmentation due to long-lived allocations + churn.
- Next steps: enable fragmentation/compaction metrics, capture allocator snapshots, and evaluate canary runtime-1.22 compaction feature behind flag.

Links / escalations
- Slack escalation: sources/slack/support/1768159022.json
- Runtime discussion: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1767311205.json, sources/slack/eng-runtime/1767394021.json
- Canary incident thread (later): sources/slack/incidents/1767735109.json
- Oncall procedures draft: sources/slack/eng-oncall/1767660044.json

Relevant logs (excerpt)
- 2026-01-29T19:42:11Z request_id=rwreq_01HTZ0R6GQ9P7J9Q8A model=rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct phase=decode msg="decode step stalled waiting for kv page" stall_ms=1640 kv_free_pages=12 kv_frag_ratio=0.61
- 2026-01-29T19:42:13Z request_id=rwreq_01HTZ0R6GQ9P7J9Q8A msg="kv eviction triggered" reason="alloc_fail" evicted_sequences=3 tier="dedicated" pinned_skipped=1
- 2026-01-29T19:42:18Z request_id=rwreq_01HTZ0R6GQ9P7J9Q8A msg="oom_avoided_shedding" shed_requests=2 pool=northwind-us-east-03

Dashboards (internal)
- Dedicated pool latency: Grafana > Dedicated / Pool / Request latency (p50/p95/p99) (northwind-us-east-03)
- GPU memory + allocator: Grafana > Serving runtime / KV cache health (fragmentation, free pages, evictions)
- Traces: Tracing > request exemplars filtered by request_id(s) from customer

Hypothesis
- KV cache allocator fragmentation rises during bursts; compaction/eviction currently happens at poor times, causing decode stalls and p99 spikes. Feature work in progress (runtime-1.22) expected to reduce fragmentation via budgeted compaction + tier-aware eviction.
comments: 2026-01-29 20:03 (Paula Mendes - Support): Created ticket from customer escalation. Customer reports p99 spikes up to 28s during burst windows; baseline p99 ~1.8s. Asked for 10 request IDs and approximate timestamps + confirmation of client timeouts.

2026-01-29 20:26 (Sean Gallagher - SRE): Looking at northwind-us-east-03. Confirm tail spikes align with GPU memory pressure + allocator churn. Not seeing gateway 5xx first; latency originates in runtime. Recommend enabling new kv fragmentation counters if available in their current runtime build; otherwise need a canary upgrade.

2026-01-29 21:10 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Pulled logs around 19:40–19:50Z. Seeing repeated "decode stalled waiting for kv page" and "alloc_fail" bursts. Flagging Runtime team. Linking #support thread sources/slack/support/1768159022.json.

2026-01-29 22:04 (Omar El-Sayed - KV cache TL): This looks consistent with fragmentation + poor-timing evictions. We have fragmentation metrics landing (PR-19342) and budgeted compaction in runtime-1.22 behind flag. Propose: 1) get metrics in their pool; 2) run canary on a subset of traffic; 3) keep kill-switch ready.

2026-01-30 09:18 (Allison Grant - Observability): If we can roll the metrics build, please ensure we wire: kv_frag_ratio, kv_bytes_moved_total, kv_compaction_time_ms, kv_evictions_total, and decode_stall_ms. Standard naming in Confluence page linked in ticket.

2026-01-30 13:37 (Paula Mendes - Support): Customer provided sample request IDs + confirmed top-of-hour batch causes 5–6x burst. They see client timeouts at 12s; retries amplify traffic. Customer asked if there is a near-term mitigation besides increasing capacity.

2026-01-30 14:05 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Short-term mitigation: raise prefill/decode concurrency caps slightly to reduce queueing, but may worsen memory pressure. Prefer to avoid. Suggest temporary traffic smoothing (customer-side) + we proceed with runtime canary w/ metrics and compaction flag off first.

2026-01-31 10:22 (Connor O’Brien - Release): We can cut a dedicated-pool canary build of runtime-1.22.0-rc2 for northwind-us-east-03. Default compaction flag OFF; metrics ON. Target: 5% traffic via router policy. ETA 2–3 hours after approval.

2026-01-31 12:11 (Sean Gallagher - SRE): Approval granted with guardrails: rollback if p99 worsens >20% for 10 min OR if kv_bytes_moved spikes correlate with decode stalls. See incident playbook thread sources/slack/eng-oncall/1767660044.json.

2026-01-31 16:02 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Canary deployed (5% traffic) runtime-1.22.0-rc2 with metrics enabled, compaction OFF. Observing kv_frag_ratio rising to ~0.58 during bursts (baseline ~0.25). Evictions also spike (alloc_fail). Confirms fragmentation hypothesis.

2026-02-01 09:44 (Omar El-Sayed - KV cache TL): Next step: enable compaction flag with conservative budget (bytes/time) on canary only. Recommendation: compaction_budget_ms_per_tick=0.3ms, max_bytes_moved_per_s=256MB, trigger_frag_ratio=0.45. Ensure kill-switch config propagation is verified first (PR-19422).

2026-02-01 11:20 (Benji Okafor - Rollout/Flags): Kill-switch propagation validated in us-east (config commit -> runtime acknowledged in ~35s). Safe-disable semantics: stops scheduling new compaction steps; in-flight relocation completes per-step then halts. (See platform thread sources/slack/eng-platform/1768080411.json.)

2026-02-01 13:08 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Enabled compaction on canary (5%). Immediate effect: kv_frag_ratio peaks lower (~0.42) and returns to baseline faster post-burst. p99 improved during 14:00Z burst window (canary cohort p99 3.1s vs control 11.6s). No throughput drop detected at p50. Logging exemplar traces added (PR-19405) for correlation.

2026-02-02 08:57 (Paula Mendes - Support): Updated customer: we identified root cause as allocator fragmentation under bursty mixed-length traffic; we have mitigation in canary that is improving p99 materially. Customer agrees to keep current capacity and retest after we expand canary.

2026-02-03 17:31 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Hit an edge case during higher churn test (cancelled requests) causing transient allocator leak suspicion. Runtime patched via PR-19440. We paused canary expansion pending patch; compaction remained ON for 5% cohort with no customer-visible incident.

2026-02-04 12:26 (Connor O’Brien - Release): runtime-1.22.1 hotfix with cancellation fix is ready for dedicated canary. Plan: upgrade canary nodes, keep compaction ON w/ conservative budgets, expand to 25% if stable for 24h.

2026-02-05 15:18 (Sean Gallagher - SRE): After 24h on 25%: p99 improved ~55–70% during bursts; no OOM/forced shedding. Eviction rate down; decode stalls reduced. Proceeding to 100% within Northwind pool with rollback window open. Alert tuning notes tracked separately in sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/kv-compaction-alert-tuning-notes.json.

2026-02-06 10:42 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Rolled to 100% of northwind-us-east-03. Observed top-of-hour burst: p99 2.7s (prev 12–28s). kv_frag_ratio stays <0.45 with compaction. No capacity changes needed.

2026-02-07 09:10 (Paula Mendes - Support): Customer confirms p99 stable across three burst windows; remaining issue is occasional client-side timeout at 12s on rare long-context requests (expected). Customer requested a summary + plan for making this default for Dedicated tiers.

2026-02-08 14:30 (Omar El-Sayed - KV cache TL): Summarized internally: compaction + tier-aware eviction will roll out broadly in runtime-1.22 with staged guardrails. This ticket can be resolved; follow-ups tracked in SUP-28472 for canary regression handling and INT-11904 for dashboard defaults.
resolution: Root cause confirmed as KV cache allocator fragmentation under bursty mixed-length workloads causing allocation stalls + poorly-timed evictions, leading to decode stalls and p99 spikes. Mitigation deployed by upgrading Northwind’s dedicated pool to runtime-1.22.1 (canary -> 100%) with fragmentation metrics enabled and budgeted KV compaction turned on (conservative budget/thresholds) plus cancellation edge-case fix. Post-rollout: burst p99 reduced from 12–28s to ~2.7–3.5s; forced shedding/OOM-avoid events eliminated during observed bursts.
next_steps: Keep compaction enabled for Northwind dedicated pool; maintain kill-switch readiness during first 2 weeks post-rollout.
Share customer-facing summary + guidance on client timeout expectations for rare long-context outliers (PM-611 link tracked outside Jira).
Ensure dashboards include kv_frag_ratio, kv_bytes_moved_total, kv_evictions_total, and decode_stall_ms panels by default (tracked in INT-11904).
Continue staged rollout of runtime-1.22 compaction defaults across other dedicated pools; watch for regressions (SUP-28472).
